chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿAlī ibn ʿAṭiyyah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
Ṣubḥ is that which, when I see it, spreads across the horizon as though it were the whiteness of the river of Sūrāʾ.

key_terms.الصُّبْحُ: the dawn meant here as true dawn marking the prayer time
key_terms.بَيَاضُ: whiteness or bright light appearing at dawn
key_terms.رَأَيْتُهُ: I observe it visually as a sign for determining the time
key_terms.سُورَاءَ: Sūrāʾ, the named river used for comparison
key_terms.نَهَرِ: river, used here in a simile
key_terms.يَعْتَرِضُ: it spreads horizontally across the horizon

ai.seo_question: How is true dawn identified for the time of salat al-fajr?
ai.summary: This hadith defines the true dawn as the light that spreads laterally across the horizon. Its significance in fiqh is that it indicates the beginning of the time for salat al-fajr.
